title: Token-provenance signalboard and staged failover panels
creator: Liang Chen
description:
Goal: Build a coarse-to-fine observability surface that ties token-level latency SLIs to routing/circuit state and multi-region failover actions. The signalboard will help SRE and oncall quickly: 1) determine whether slow requests are due to model decode cost, KV cache misses, or routing/fallback; 2) validate circuit-breaker triggers and load-shedding effectiveness across regions; 3) quantify user-facing impact in token-time and requests-at-risk so Product and Support can triage proactively.

Scope:
- Instrumentation: emit token-level timing spans (decode.start, decode.end, kv.lookup.hit|miss, admit.decide, reroute.start/end, circuit.state) with a stable set of trace tags: model, model_version, region, shard_id, route, tenant_id (hashed), request_cohort. These are lightweight aggregated metrics and sampled traces for tail analysis.
- SLIs/SLOs: define token-latency SLIs (p50/p95/p99 per region/model/version over tokens emitted), KV hit-rate SLI, admit ratio SLI, and failover latency SLI (time between primary region failover decision and first token emitted from fallback).
- Dashboard buildout: a multi-tab Grafana dashboard with: Overview (golden-signal rollup and current SLO burn), Token Provenance panel (stacked waterfall showing token time contributions), Circuit State Timeline (per-tenant aggregated circuit transitions), Multi-region Failover Replay (sequence diagram + table of affected requests), and Playbook Panel (runbook quick-links & recent run actions).
- Acceptance criteria:
  * Token-latency SLI emits continuous aggregates at 1m resolution with p50/p95/p99, backing SLO alerting.
  * Waterfall panel can attribute >90% of tail token time to one of: decode, kv-miss penalty, routing latency, or queueing.
  * Failover replay can reconstruct 95% of multi-region routed requests for the previous 7 days given sampled traces.
  * Dashboards have owner and are linked from console incident workflow.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Sampling vs full telemetry: full per-token traces high cardinality -> we will emit low-overhead aggregated histograms per minute and keep a 0.1% sampled full-span trace for tail debugging. This reduces ingestion cost and keeps SLI accuracy for p95/p99 within an acceptable error margin (measured in the spec).
- Tag set: adding tenant_id hashing reduces privacy risk while allowing per-tenant SLO slicing. We avoid recording prompt content or user identifiers.
- Storage window: keep fine-grained histograms for 30 days and pre-aggregated rollups for 90 days to support med-term incident forensics.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrument runtime decode and routing hooks to emit lightweight metrics and span markers (ENG tasks: runtime-hooking).
2) Implement histogram aggregator in metrics pipeline (Metrica) producing token-latency p50/p95/p99 per minute.
3) Dashboard panels: mock in Grafana (link attached), then review with SRE and PM.
4) Alerts & Runbook: create SLOs and oncall playbooks; wire to PagerDuty for P0 burn.

Stakeholders and reviewers: Marco Gutierrez (runtime), Sara O'Neill (SRE lead), Priya Rao (PM), Design TBD for dashboard UX.

Notes: this ticket focuses on instrumentation and dashboard design; follow-up tickets will implement automatic mitigation (adaptive admission changes) based on these signals.
